We're talking took most of everything leaving only the last bit of his half of rent and a few things he said in a note he didn't want to bring with him. Thing with where I live is that if you don't discard of things on your own when you move out the landlord can pay to have someone remove the stuff. We're talking cases of dudes having $250 taken off their deposit just for some dude to take 3 milk crates of things to the dump. It's a rip off. I texted and emailed him for 2 weeks asking to pick these things up or take them to the dump but he never responded. So I took most of his things to the dump but he also had around 60 video games for PS4. So I figured I'd sell them. There is a local game store where they buy used games and they gave me $600 for all of his games. Well cut to last week and I was at a party he was at and we were polite. He then asks how the move out was and I said good, and naturally he asked what I did with his stuff. He got mad when he found out I sold his games but I told him that I tried to get him to grab these things but he never reached out. He's now calling me an asshole and asking me to pay him back. I checked and legally there's nothing there but now I'm wondering if I'm the asshole for doing this.

Answer: <0 or 1>

prediction.raw: 0 I think you're not the asshole in this scenario. Here's why: 1. **Abandonment**: Your former roommate abandoned his belongings, including the video games, without making any arrangements for their disposal or retrieval. 2. **Repeated attempts to contact**: You made multiple attempts to reach out to him via text and email, giving him ample opportunity to claim his belongings or make arrangements for their disposal. 3. **Landlord's policy**: You were aware of the landlord's policy regarding abandoned belongings and the potential financial consequences of not disposing of them properly. 4. **Reasonable action**: Given the circumstances, selling the video games to a local game store was a reasonable action to take, especially since you were able to recoup some value from them. 5. **No legal obligation**: You've checked and found that there's no legal obligation for you to pay him back, which suggests that your actions were within your rights as a tenant. While it's understandable that your former roommate might be upset about the situation, his anger and demand for repayment seem unwarranted. He had ample opportunity to claim his belongings or make arrangements for their disposal, and his failure to do so doesn't make you responsible for his losses. It's worth noting that your former roommate's behavior, including abandoning his belongings and not responding to your attempts to contact him, suggests a lack of responsibility and accountability. In contrast, you took reasonable steps to dispose of his belongings and even tried to reach out to him to give him the opportunity to claim them. Overall, it seems that you acted in good faith and within your rights, and you're not the asshole in this scenario.
